# #204 correctness review: PASS-WITH-NOTES

Head: `75be9c2fdd4534883ae4ed49c1392fef5c010804`.
Request: `01a1bead-aa5e-7a23-b7ba-ce84a8cb1d9b`.
Read-only review against `7f6ed760ed98b2fda2e6095750a6e8f620132f8f`, under C33/C34. Worktree clean and pinned. No local builds, tests or mutants.

**F150 is closed. No normal-use correctness bug found.**

- Qualification excludes `reply = 'none'` from the existing delivered/unanswered request query. The conditional mark independently repeats that predicate, so changing the request to reply-none between qualification and mark refuses a request-only nudge.
- The directory's `UNANSWERED_SQL` uses the same exclusion and remains connected to the two-live-holders action through `unanswered_by_holder`. Its test retains wake/fyi positives while reply-none contributes no count. Time-limit/check-in SQL is unchanged.
- Requests group by the raw role, instance and project tuple, so distinct addresses/projects are not collapsed merely because their rendered names match. The group count and minimum delivery timestamp produce the single counted label and oldest age; the mark retains all original request ids, not rendered labels.
- Shared notice joining applies the 1,500-byte item budget and reports omitted **items/groups**, not an invented count of omitted requests. Separator/summary text adds small overhead beyond that item budget; the complete nudge and both FYI forms remain below 2,048 bytes for the bounded labels produced here. The first-item exception does not create an oversized normal-use notice because holding/claim/request labels render bounded identities and numeric fields.
- The 40-request daemon test proves one grouped label. The long-list core test checks all three complete notice bodies, including the omitted-item count and canonical label/age positive.

**Known limit:** F161 time-limit alert grouping remains open with delivery; it is not claimed by `Fixes: F150`.

All five latest checks succeeded. Head-bound CI run `42564236452`, attempt 1, and matching JUnit evidence show **2317 passing cases**, zero failures/errors; nextest separately reports **five skips**. All five changed/new requirement tests and the indexed directory-count test are present and passed. Mutants were skipped as permitted by C34.

No new read, periodic loop or launch. Existing queries gain predicates and one delivery-time column; grouping and capped joining run in process. The merge has no remerge conflict delta.

Evidence: `pr204-75be9c2.diff`, `pr204-75be9c2-junit.xml`, `pr204-75be9c2-ci.log`.

**Handback:** PASS-WITH-NOTES at this exact head; retain F161 as the explicit separate limitation.
